text:
ci-bot: [CI] PR 13250 - perf bench failure detected: `kv_cache_hit` microbench regressed 12.7% (threshold 5%). See build: https://ci.redwood/internal/13250 
ci-bot: metrics snapshot:
```
kv_cache_hit: baseline=1.02ms, head=1.15ms, delta=12.7%
kv_warmup: hit_rate baseline=78%, head=66%
```
maria: ugh, assigning to perf triage. tagging @sam and @hugo
sam: starting local repro. can someone paste the exact bench command that failed in CI?
ci-bot: command: `./scripts/bench --suite kv_cache_hit --runs 20 --bench-config ci.json`
sam: running that now locally, attaching short profile in a sec
sam: local run: median token latency 1.18ms (consistent with CI). warmup shows kv hit drop around iteration 3-4
hugo: ping — PR 13245 merged yesterday touched kernel selector + batching heuristic (selector refactor). could be related
maria: if selector changed, it could prefer a different kernel with worse prefetch / quantized path perf. please check kernel names in traces
sam: flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/fg/3899990000 — shows hot path in `kernel_y::prefetch_loop` vs `kernel_x::vector_copy` previously
perf-bot: starting automated bisect across commits 13245..HEAD (CI bisect harness)
sam: manual quick check: `python -m tests.microbench.kv --seq 512 --runs 10`
```
before (commit before 13245): median=1.03ms
after (HEAD): median=1.18ms
```
kevin: can you narrow to the exact commit in 13245? which file changed?
hugo: commit abc1234 inside PR 13245 changed kernel_selector.py: the cost model threshold lowered, and we added an early-bail that picks `kernel_y` for quantized convs when batch_size <= 8
sam: git bisect results (quick CI-assisted run): culprit commit = abc1234 (PR 13245) — confirmed on two GPUs
maria: ok looks reproducible. options: revert 13245, or hotfix the selector rule to avoid picking kernel_y for seq < 1024 / quantized path
hugo: I prefer hotfix: the change was aimed at throughput cases but regressed short-seq tail latency. patching selection logic to reintroduce a seq-length guard should be quick
kevin: filing PR 13260 with selector guard, small change in `kernel_selector.py`
sam: testing 13260 locally...
sam: after applying selector guard:
```
median=1.05ms (within noise), kv hit rate restored to 77%
```
maria: nice. can we run CI perf harness on 13260 and confirm? mark it as urgent/rollout-blocker if green
perf-bot: queued perf CI for PR 13260 — running microbench suites (kv, batcher, warmup)
perf-bot: CI perf results for 13260: all metrics within ±2% of baseline. kv_cache_hit delta: +0.6%
sam: updating PR with bench snapshots and the flamegraph comparison
maria: I'll merge hotfix to main and patch release branch. also creating a revert PR for 13245 in case we need full rollback
hugo: follow-up TODO: revisit selector cost model, add unit test that covers short-seq quantized path to catch this earlier
kevin: added test+comment in PR 13260, link: https://git.redwood/13260
maria: marking this incident as resolved — rollout-blocker cleared :thumbsup: :rotating_light: 
perf-bot: post-merge CI perf sweep on main: green
kevin: leaving notes in the release changelog about the heuristic tweak
maria: thanks everyone, closing thread. ping if it reappears.
